To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in the developing countries, the care of HIV-infected people, especially women and children, is inadequate and that the authorities and the population in general are unaware of the problem.
the care of HIV-infected persons and their families is of great importance and that it is a matter of urgency to improve the quality and availability of care in the developing countries.

in developing countries there is a need to: 1) provide a basic infrastructure for care; 2) provide a framework for care; 3) develop a care system for children; 4) develop a system for the care of orphans; 5) develop a care network for women; and 6) develop a system of care for the elderly.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the synthesis of biologically active compounds and the investigation of their biological properties.
the development of an instrument for the evaluation of the quality of care for people with HIV infection/AIDS.

the following issues: (i) the epidemiology of HIV infection and AIDS; (ii) the social and psychological problems of patients and their families; (iii) the organisation of care; and (iv) the development and evaluation of interventions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the care of HIV-infected people and their families is still in its infancy in many parts of the world.
the care of HIV-infected patients in the developing world is inadequate.
the world has to do more and better to improve the care of HIV-infected people.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the international community must do its best to improve the situation of HIV-infected people in the developing countries.
we have to do more than ever, and that we should not forget that our patients are people with feelings, with needs and with dignity.
we have to take better care of our patients and their families, and we must also help the less fortunate people in developing countries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have to take care of our patients, not only in our own countries but also in developing countries.
the care of HIV-infected patients is a worldwide task.
the patient's own family and social network is the most important source of support.
